narration: Lars spent all his birthday money. At home, he watches his big brother Senna count his bills and coins. Senna earned it walking dogs in the neighborhood. "It's a great way to make some money," Senna says.
image_brief: Lars sitting on the edge of a bed, watching his big brother Senna count dog-walking money into a jar at home.

narration: Lars kept his $5 safe today. That night, he thinks about Senna's dog walking. He decides to start his own business: a lemonade stand!
image_brief: Lars at his desk at night, drawing a lemonade stand in his notebook, a $5 bill beside him.

narration: Senna's birthday is on Saturday, and Lars has a plan. He's going to get Senna the cool phone case from the store window. There's just one problem...
image_brief: Lars outside a store window, pointing at a phone case on display, his wallet in his other hand.

narration: Lars asks Mom if he can earn some extra money before Saturday. Mom hands him a chore list. "Get these done by Friday, and they're worth $10."
image_brief: Lars and Mom in the kitchen, Mom handing Lars a chore list, Lars looking keen.

narration: Senna loves his new phone case. That night, Lars tells Mom his big dream: swapping his old bike for a better mountain bike. His parents say they'll help, but Lars has to pay for part of it himself. Pocket money won't get him there, so Lars makes a plan.
image_brief: Lars and Mom talking at the kitchen table in the evening, Lars excited, a picture of a mountain bike in his mind.

narration: Lars wants to run a lemonade stand. First he needs a jug, paper cups, lemons, sugar and ingredients to bake cookies. That all costs money, so he decides to save for it. Mom agrees, as long as the stand goes by their front gate, where she can see him.
image_brief: Lars writing his startup list (jug, cups, lemons, sugar) while Mom reads over his shoulder, smiling.

narration: Saving for the lemonade stand idea sounds easy, but he keeps spending his money at the corner store. The weeks fly by. Then one afternoon, Lars borrows Senna's headphones...
image_brief: Lars on the couch wearing his big brother Senna's headphones, a snack wrapper beside him.

narration: Lars finds an old jam jar and writes 'Emergencies' on the lid to save for when things go wrong. It's only a jar, but it's a start. Every time he gets money, some goes in. Next time something breaks, he'll be ready.
image_brief: Lars at his desk, writing 'Emergencies' on the lid of an old jam jar, a few coins beside it.

narration: The headphones are replaced, but Lars's startup money is still $0. "Before you buy something, ask if you really want or need it," says his school friend Mason. "That's how I've saved so much."
image_brief: Lars and his school friend Mason eating lunch in the school yard, Mason giving advice with a calm shrug.

narration: One afternoon, Lars's friends all ping him. A new skin has dropped on their favorite game. A limited time offer and the countdown is ticking. Lars remembers Mason's words. His startup money is still $0.
image_brief: Lars and Mason at lunch in the school yard, friends around them staring at their phones.

narration: After school, Lars walks home past the shops. Every window seems to be shouting at him.
image_brief: Lars walking past a row of shop windows full of bright sale signs.

narration: Lars grabs an envelope to keep the money for his lemonade stand separate. He writes 'Startup money needed: $15' on the front.
image_brief: Lars at his desk writing 'Startup money needed: $15' on an envelope, coins stacked beside it.

narration: He tucks the envelope away. $10 saved, $5 to go. He pictures his stand by the front gate, with a bright sign and a jug of lemonade.
image_brief: Lars tucking the envelope into a drawer, with a dreamy thought bubble of his lemonade stand by the front gate.

narration: It's Mia's birthday! She's invited Lars to the gelato shop after school to celebrate.
image_brief: Lars and his friend Mia walking together after school, Mia wearing a birthday badge.

narration: At the shop, the counter is a rainbow of flavors. Mia picks hers straight away. Lars looks at the cups and his tummy rumbles.
image_brief: Lars and Mia at a gelato counter full of colorful flavors, Mia pointing at hers.

narration: Lars and Mia share the birthday gelato. She's happy Lars came along, and Lars is grateful for Mia's generosity. He decides to repay the favor to Mia when he can. His startup envelope still holds $10.
image_brief: Lars and Mia leaving the gelato shop, sharing one gelato with two spoons, Mia in a birthday badge.

narration: A week later, the movie everyone's talking about hits the cinema. Mia has an idea.
image_brief: Mia talking excitedly to Lars, a movie poster on the wall behind them.

narration: Friday night, Mom and Lars meet Mia at the cinema. The smell of popcorn hits them at the door.
image_brief: Lars, Mom and Mia arriving at a cinema entrance at night, a popcorn stand inside.

narration: Lars paid his own half. No borrowing, no stress. His startup money stayed at $10, and he still has $3 spare.
image_brief: Lars and Mia waiting in line at the movie theater, tickets in hand, Lars looking relaxed.

narration: While they wait, Mia doodles a lemon on her ticket. "I could design the sign for your stand," she says.
image_brief: Close-up of Mia doodling a lemon on her movie ticket while Lars grins.

narration: At the bus stop, Lars shares some big news with Mason. Mom told the neighbors about his lemonade stand idea, and lots of them want to buy some!
image_brief: Lars and Mason at the school bus stop, Lars excitedly sharing his news, Mason listening.

narration: Two straws, one slushie, and $1 still in Lars's pocket. "Deals like that used to get me every time," Lars laughs.
image_brief: Lars and Mia sharing one slushie with two straws, Lars laughing.

narration: Saturday morning. Lars and his friends are going to the mall. Lars looks at the note and picture above his desk: 'Mountain bike'. He decides to leave the money for his startup at home.
image_brief: Lars at his desk on a sunny morning, looking at a note on his wall that says 'Mountain bike'.

narration: Lars has two weeks of pocket money, $10, at the mall. And what he does with the money he brought, is up to you! Let's see the choices Lars has to make today.
image_brief: Lars heading out the front door with a small wallet, waving to Mom.

narration: With $15 in his envelope, Lars buys a jug, cups, lemons and sugar. Mia's sign goes on the front. On Saturday, his stand opens by the front gate. He's one step closer to his mountain bike!
image_brief: Lars at his new lemonade stand by the front gate, Mia's sign on the front, Mom watching from the porch.
